result:
Solution 2 is wrong. Its ideal (x, y², z) is not integrally closed, since y ∈ \overline{I}, and its logic about vacuous truth does not address the actual question.

Solution 3 is also wrong. It derives 3 from a heuristic claim that non-normal examples appear only with at least 5 generators. That claim does not support its stopping point at 3, because it says the 4-generator case is already normal.

Solution 1 gives 5. I did not derive this myself. It rests on my recollection of a published result that integrally closed height-3 monomial ideals in k[x,y,z] with at most 5 generators are normal, with a non-normal example at 6 generators. I am not fully certain of that recollection. Its citation (Hoa–Stückrad–Vogel, 1996) looks doubtful, but the final value matches what I recall.

CHOICE: 1
